analysis_type: Post-hoc synthesis of existing frozen outputs with a shared diagnostic kernel; no refitting and no new independent experiment

normalization_rule.hahn1: Recompute the shared 1001-grid prediction-domain check on each frozen fold's held-out points; derive minimal local numerical identifiability from numerical rank 7 and finite positive standard errors; mark every fold as post_hoc_gate_reconstruction
normalization_rule.thurber: Reuse the frozen dataset-prospective domain and identifiability decisions and all five fold metrics
normalization_rule.kirby2: Reuse the frozen dataset-prospective domain and identifiability decisions and all five fold metrics
normalization_rule.baseline: Hahn1 and Thurber use cubic polynomial baselines; Kirby2 uses its frozen quadratic polynomial baseline
normalization_rule.fold_gate_consistent: Prediction-domain admissible AND minimal local numerical identifiability AND model RMSE <= the fold's frozen baseline RMSE
normalization_rule.dataset_all_folds: All five folds are gate-consistent; preserve the original assessment type and do not relabel post-hoc reconstruction as prospective

prohibitions: No new fitting, model selection, threshold retuning or deletion of failures
No interpretation of fold counts as a universal detection accuracy or model-family ranking
No merging of post-hoc Hahn1 reconstruction with the stronger dataset-prospective evidence labels
No claim of independent physical experiments, global identifiability or parameter endogeneity
